attempts.sql: SELECT regexp_extract(file_id, '^(auto_ontology/server/[^/]+)/', 1) AS folder_path, CAST(SUM(line_count) AS INTEGER) AS total_lines FROM auto_ontology_code.code.files WHERE regexp_matches(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/[^/]+/.+[.]py$') GROUP BY folder_path HAVING SUM(line_count) > 1000 ORDER BY total_lines DESC, folder_path ASC;

request:
Within auto_ontology/server/, which immediate subfolders contain more than 1,000 lines of Python in total? Count every .py file anywhere inside the subfolder, including its test files and __init__.py; files directly in auto_ontology/server/ itself belong to no subfolder. Return the subfolder's repository-relative path (e.g. auto_ontology/server/chat) and its total line count.

Requested output columns: folder_path (string), total_lines (integer).
Return exactly the requested output columns, using each requested name as the column alias, in the requested order. Return complete repository-relative file paths and complete symbol IDs exactly as stored. When the question asks which files, symbols or modules, return each distinct one once unless it asks for occurrences.
explanation: This calculates total Python lines for each immediate subfolder under auto_ontology/server. It uses each file's repository-relative path to identify the immediate subfolder and sums the stored line counts for every matching .py file, including test files and __init__.py files. Files directly inside auto_ontology/server are excluded, and only subfolders whose summed line count exceeds 1,000 are returned.
sql: SELECT regexp_extract(file_id, '^(auto_ontology/server/[^/]+)/', 1) AS folder_path, CAST(SUM(line_count) AS INTEGER) AS total_lines FROM auto_ontology_code.code.files WHERE regexp_matches(file_id, '^auto_ontology/server/[^/]+/.+[.]py$') GROUP BY folder_path HAVING SUM(line_count) > 1000 ORDER BY total_lines DESC, folder_path ASC;
